In this lesson, you will learn about motion.
INTRODUCTIONM
If you are going 55 mph, you are using the terms associated with motion.
Distance can be given in any absolute term. Examples are inches, feet, miles, meters, etc..
Distance can be given in relative terms. Examples are machine cycles, revolutions, strokes, etc.
Time can also be given in many forms. Examples are seconds, minutes, hours, days, etc.
In motion, a change in the position of an object over time is important.
Let's begin the lesson on NATURE IN MOTION................................

CIRCULAR MOTIONITLE
Circular motion is the motion produced by rotating machines, motors for example.
DISCUSSION
In fact, most industrial applications first produce motion by motors, circular motion, and then change it to linear motion.
The changing between circular and linear motion is accomplished by a rack and pinion.
Circular motion is normally measured in rotations (or revolutions) per minute, RPM.
RPM is the number of complete rotations, 360 degree movements, that occur each minute.
RPM is velocity. Rotation is a relative term for distance. Minutes is a term for time.
A change in RPM (velocity) causes acceleration or deceleration.
What happens to velocity during deceleration?
Linear velocity is motion in a straight line. Circular motion is like the shaft of a spinning motor.
TRY AGAIN!
RPM is a measure of circular motion........................
TRY AGAIN!
The problem with using RPM as velocity is that it is a relative term.
In most applications, you need to describe circular velocity and circular distance in absolute terms, like ft/sec and feet.
Changing RPM to absolute terms is done by calculating: runout rate (ROR) and runout distance (ROD).
Runout is a term used to describe the method of changing circular motion to linear motion.
Consider that a rotating shaft will cause a plate to move..
Point A is the initial position on the shaft.
Point a is the initial position on the plate. Notice these points are where the shaft and plate touch.
Now, as the shaft rotates to points B, the plate also moves to point b.
The distance between point a and point b of the plate is the distance that the shaft rotated is called runout........
As the shaft continues to rotate to point C, the plate continues to move.
The distance the plate moved is now from point a to point c.
At point D, the shaft has moved more causing the plate to move more.
Finally, when the shaft returns to point A, the distance from A to a on the shaft and the distance from A to a on the plate is the same.
You can now measure the distance on the plate from A to a in feet, inches, or meters, in absolute terms.
The circular motion was changed into linear motion.........
Now, you can determine velocity and distance in absolute terms.
The formula for determining the runout rate, velocity or ROR, is simple. You multiply the RPM times the circumference of the shaft.
Recall that the circumference is the distance around a circle, or shaft.
RPM is the number of complete rotations in a minute.
So, if a shaft has a circumference of 10 inches and is moving at 10 RPM, the ROR is 100 inches/minutes. This is velocity.
What is the ROR of a motor that has a RPM of 60 and has a shaft with the circumference of 2 inches?
60 is the RPM of the motor. To find the velocity, or runout rate, you must multiply RPM by the circumference of the shaft..

The units of measure are not in feet and seconds. RPM is minutes and the circumference is inches.
TRY AGAIN!
VELOCITY OR RUNOUT RATE - The velocity of circular motion equals the RPM of the object times the circumference of the object.
Normally, the velocity of most circular motion devices is calculated in ft/sec.
Normally the radius is given instead of circumference......
So, this formula is the one that you will normally use.....
Two pi r is used to calculate the circumference of the device when the radius is given, and r should be in feet.
Dividing by 60 changes rotations per minute, RPM, to rotations per second.
For example, if a motor has an RPM of 1500 and has a shaft radius of .03 feet, the velocity or ROR is 4.71 ft/sec.

INCHES - The radius of the shaft is given in inches. To find velocity in ft/sec, you must change inches to feet.

Since ROR is circular velocity that has been changed to linear velocity, the circular distance equals ROR multiplied by time.
